correctness.rationale: The SVD yields the product characteristic function; \(r\ge2\) has integrable Fourier transform and hence continuous positive origin density. Joint iid-density ball scaling yields the exact leading constant. At \(r=1\), the K0 origin expansion with an integrable product-of-logarithms dominator gives the exact log-power coefficient. The p-th moment tail-integral criterion proves the boundary including \(p=\ell\). Jensen strict concavity for squared singular-value weights gives the exact unique fixed-rank minimizer, while \(\log(1+u)<u\) gives strict full-Gaussian comparison. The flat-spectrum beta integral and Laplace rank-two example were reconstructed. The packaged verifier passed 38 finite checks; infinite assertions rest on proof, not experiments.

originality.rationale: The inspected numerical-analysis papers establish tensor-probe estimators, general nonasymptotic bounds, the one-probe product-normal obstruction, and the qualitative disappearance of its logarithmic singularity at matrix rank at least two. They do not supply the exact multi-probe Euclidean-ball coefficients indexed by all nonzero singular values, the unique spectrum-constrained minimizer, or the sharp inverse-moment classification for this precise independent-pair observable. A related earlier coefficient-error ratio involves a random numerator and does not imply the full matrix-rank constant theorem. Priority outside inspected sources remains uncertain.
residual_risks: An exact Fourier-density small-ball formula or equivalent extremality theorem may have appeared in probability literature under decoupled Gaussian chaos or variance-gamma terminology; no independent priority audit was performed.

The rank-one logarithmic mechanism and \(r\ge2\) qualitative log removal are already known; novelty rests on the explicit all-rank all-ell constants, spectral extremality, and resulting inverse-moment classification for independent probes.
The analysis is restricted to independent real factor pairs and fixed separable residuals; it cannot be transferred unmodified to the 2026 shared-factor matrix-block statistic.

value.rationale: The motivating independent validation-sketch problem asks how many cheap tensor-factor probes are needed not to miss a fixed residual. An exact leading probability coefficient and sharp inverse-moment threshold determine this numerical reliability beyond loose confidence bounds; the singular-spectrum optimizer describes a nontrivial worst-case dependence and a provable factor pi cost at rank two with two probes compared with dense probing. The previously known qualitative logarithmic rank transition is not alone the value: the new finite-rank constants, strict extremal matrix classification, and spectral-collapse nonuniformity form a motivated complete asymptotic calculation. The spatial operator of the separable residual has stable rank one even when its reshaped coefficient matrix has rank at least two, so the matrix-rank-sensitive leading constants address information absent from stable-rank-only guarantees.
